html:
Nejd is the high central plateau of Arabia, around modern Riyadh. On the map, from 1783 to 1815, it is the Emirate of Diriyah, the first Saudi state.

Before then Nejd was a land of small oasis towns and Bedouin tribes, each with its own chief. In 1744 the ruler of the town of Diriyah, Muhammad bin Saud, made a pact with the preacher Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, who called for a strict return to early Islam. The Saudis gave the movement a sword and the preacher gave the Saudis a cause.

By 1800 the emirate held most of Nejd and eastern Arabia. In 1803 and 1805 it took Mecca and Medina in the Hejaz, a direct challenge to the Ottoman sultan. The Ottomans sent Muhammad Ali of Egypt against it. His army destroyed Diriyah in 1818. The Saudis came back twice, and the third Saudi state became Saudi Arabia in 1932.
sum: Nejd is the high central plateau of Arabia, around modern Riyadh. On the map, from 1783 to 1815, it is the Emirate of Diriyah, the first Saudi state.
